_about: Table IA.VIII, Signal Definitions and Citations. One row per column of the 145-column Stage-2 panel: 108 sorted signals plus 37 identifiers, returns and characteristics. Extracted from the paper's longtable, then reconciled against Stage 2's DATA_DICTIONARY.md and the code that computes each signal. A row carrying `paper_prints` or `paper_prints_citation` is one where the two disagreed and the code settled it; `why_corrected` says what settled it. Everything else is the paper's text unchanged. See RECONCILIATION_ia08.md.

rows.name: Bond Identifier
rows.description: 9-digit CUSIP bond identifier.

rows.name: Date
rows.description: True month-end date (YYYY-MM-DD).

rows.name: Issuer CUSIP

rows.name: CRSP PERMNO
rows.description: CRSP permanent security identifier.

rows.name: CRSP PERMCO
rows.description: CRSP permanent company identifier.

rows.name: Compustat GVKEY
rows.description: Compustat global company key.

rows.name: Holding Period
rows.description: Month-end holding period in calendar days (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}).

rows.name: Latent Implementation Bias
rows.description: Clean price return from month-end to month-begin: $\text{LIB} = P_t^{\text{bgn}} / P_{t-1}^{\text{end}} - 1$ (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}).

rows.name: LIB (Dirty)
rows.description: LIB computed using dirty prices (includes accrued interest and coupon).

rows.name: Return Type
rows.description: Return classification: standard, trad_in_def, or default_evnt.

rows.name: FF17 Industry
rows.description: Fama-French 17-industry classification.

rows.name: FF30 Industry
rows.description: Fama-French 30-industry classification.

rows.name: Market Cap (Start)
rows.description: Bond market capitalization at end of month $t{-}1$.

rows.name: Market Cap (End)
rows.description: Bond market capitalization at end of month $t$.

rows.name: Treasury Return
rows.description: Duration-matched U.S. Treasury portfolio return. Used to compute duration-adjusted returns: $r^x = r - tret$.

rows.name: Treasury Return, Duration-Weighted Cash Flows
rows.description: Treasury benchmark built from the bond's own cash flows, weighted by their present-value shares (Macaulay duration weights) and applied to zero-coupon Treasury returns from the Gurkaynak-Sack-Wright curve. Subtract from `ret_vw` for a duration-adjusted return.

rows.name: Treasury Return, Cash-Flow-Weighted
rows.description: As `tret_bns`, but weighting the same cash flows by their future value rather than their present value. Places more weight on long-dated cash flows and so overstates a bond's interest rate risk; reported as the authors' own robustness alternative.
rows.citation: van Binsbergen, Nozawa, and Schwert (2025), Internet Appendix A1
rows.citation_text: van Binsbergen, Nozawa, and Schwert (2025), Internet Appendix A1

rows.name: Treasury Return, Exact Duration Match
rows.description: As `tret_bns`, refined so the Treasury portfolio's duration equals the bond's exactly. The present-value weights are duration-matched only when the term structure is flat; this solves for the Treasury yield that restores the match and reweights accordingly.
rows.citation: Ghaderi, Plante, Roussanov, and Seo (2026), Appendix B.2
rows.citation_text: Ghaderi, Plante, Roussanov, and Seo (2026), Appendix B.2

rows.name: Treasury Return, Cash-Flow-Matched
rows.description: As `tret_bns`, but discounting the same cash flows on the Treasury zero curve instead of at the bond's own yield to maturity. This replicates the bond's cash flows rather than its duration, so it removes slope and curvature effects as well as parallel shifts. The difference from `tret_bns` is the authors' higher-order component.

rows.name: Treasury Return, Maturity-Matched
rows.description: The twin of `tret`: the same key-rate Treasury index returns, the same interpolation nodes and rounding, but interpolated at the bond's remaining MATURITY rather than its modified duration. Included as the maturity-matched comparator; duration matching is the more precise of the two.

rows.name: Total Return (End)
rows.description: Month-end to month-end total return (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}).

rows.name: Total Return (Begin)
rows.description: Month-begin to month-end total return within the same month (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}).

rows.name: Date Start
rows.description: Trade date for month-end price in month $t{-}1$ (last 5 BD); refer to Panel A of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Date End
rows.description: Trade date for month-end price in month $t$ (last 5 BD); refer to Panel A of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Date Start (Begin)
rows.description: Trade date for month-begin price in month $t$ (first 5 BD); refer to Panel C of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Date End (Begin)
rows.description: Trade date for month-end price in month $t$ (last 5 BD) for begin returns; refer to Panel C of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Holding Period (Begin)
rows.description: Month-begin holding period in calendar days.

rows.name: Implementation Gap
rows.description: Business days between month-end price ($t{-}1$) and month-begin price ($t$); capped at 5 BD. Refer to Panel D of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Signal Date
rows.description: Date when price-based signal was observed (minimum 1 BD before month-end price). Refer to Panel B of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Signal Gap
rows.description: Business days between signal observation and month-end price; ranges 1--10 BD. Refer to Panel B of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Risk-Free Rate
rows.description: Monthly risk-free rate from Fama-French. Used for excess returns: $r^x = r - r^f$.

rows.name: S&P Composite Rating
rows.description: Composite credit rating: S&P rating if available, otherwise Moody's rating. Scale: 1 (AAA) to 21 (C), 22 = Default.
rows.paper_prints: Composite credit rating: S&P rating if available, otherwise Moody's rating. Scale: 1 (AAA) to 21 (CCC-), 22 = Default.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row labels rating 21 as CCC-. On the numeric scale Stage 1 builds (stage1/helper_functions.convert_sp_to_numeric), CCC- is 19, CC is 20, C is 21 and D is 22. The scale's range is right; only the label on its last non-default grade is wrong.

rows.name: Moody's Composite Rating
rows.description: Composite credit rating: Moody's rating if available, otherwise S&P rating. Scale: 1 (Aaa) to 21 (C), 22 = Default.
rows.paper_prints: Composite credit rating: Moody's rating if available, otherwise S&P rating. Scale: 1 (AAA) to 20 (CCC-), 21 = Default.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says 1--20 with 21 = Default. Its own `spc_rat` row, one line above, says 1--21 with 22 = Default for the identical scale, and so does Stage 2's data dictionary. The paper contradicts itself; the 21/22 scale is the one the data uses. Rating 21 is C, not CCC- (CCC- and Caa3 are 19; see stage1/helper_functions.convert_sp_to_numeric and convert_moodys_to_numeric).

rows.name: Callable Indicator
rows.description: Indicator for embedded call option (1 = callable, 0 = non-callable).

rows.name: Face Value
rows.description: Bond amount outstanding (face value); units of the bond outstanding.

rows.name: Rule 144A Indicator
rows.description: Dummy variable: 1 if bond is Rule 144A, 0 otherwise.

rows.name: Country
rows.description: Country of issuance (e.g., USA for U.S. bonds).

rows.name: Time to Maturity
rows.description: Years remaining until bond maturity.

rows.name: Bond Age
rows.description: Years since bond issuance.

rows.name: Yield to Maturity
rows.description: Annualized yield to maturity. Computed with QuantLib.

rows.name: Credit Spread
rows.description: Annualized credit spread: yield minus maturity-matched U.S. Treasury yield.

rows.name: Modified Duration
rows.description: Modified duration measuring price sensitivity to yield changes. Computed with QuantLib.

rows.name: Convexity
rows.description: Second-order price sensitivity to yield changes. Computed with QuantLib.

rows.name: Bond Size
rows.description: Bond market capitalization: dirty price times amount outstanding (\$ millions).

rows.name: 6-Month Spread Narrowing (log)
rows.description: Log change in credit spread over prior 6 months: $\log(cs_{t-6}) - \log(cs_t)$. If the spread is missing exactly 6 months ago, the nearest adjacent month is used within a $\pm$1 month band, the EARLIER month first.
rows.paper_prints: Log change in credit spread over prior 6 months: $\log(cs_{t-6}) - \log(cs_t)$. If spread is missing exactly 6 months ago, the nearest adjacent spread is used within a $\pm$2 month band, with $+$ favored over $-$.
rows.why_corrected: Measured in the code, not inferred: `_stage2_settings.DSPREAD_BANDWIDTH = 1`, and `lib/value.py` builds `offsets = [0, -1, +1]`, so the search is one month either side and prefers the earlier month (the longer lag). The printed row says a $\pm$2 band with `+` favoured over `-` -- wrong in the width AND backwards in the tie-break. `dcs6` is an FDR survivor, so this is not cosmetic.

rows.name: 12-Month Average Spread
rows.description: Rolling 12-month average credit spread, skipping the prior month. Requires minimum 6 observations.

rows.name: Bond Book-to-Market
rows.description: Par price divided by market price of the bond. All bonds have a par value of \$1,000 (100%).

rows.name: Value (HZ)
rows.description: Percentage deviation of observed credit spread from fitted ``fair'' spread: $(cs - \widehat{cs}) / \widehat{cs}$. Controls: rating, industry, maturity, spread change, callable. Fitted spread is estimated each month via cross-sectional regression; because cs is used, this signal is also exposed to microstructure noise.

rows.name: Value (HZ, DtS-adjusted)
rows.description: HZ value signal demeaned within duration-times-spread quintiles to control for systematic spread-duration risk.

rows.name: Value (IPR)
rows.description: Log-spread residual from fair-value regression: $\log(cs) - X'\hat{\beta}$. Controls: rating, industry, log duration, volatility, callable. Fitted spread is estimated each month via cross-sectional regression; because cs is used, this signal is also exposed to microstructure noise.

rows.name: Value (IPR, DtS-adjusted)
rows.description: IPR value signal demeaned within duration-times-spread quintiles.

rows.name: 3-Month Momentum
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}2$ to $t{-}1$, skipping prior month.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row cites `gebhardt2005cross` -- Gebhardt, Hvidkjaer and Swaminathan (2005), *The cross-section of expected corporate bond returns: betas or characteristics?*. Bond momentum is the OTHER GHS 2005 paper, *Stock and bond market interaction: does momentum spill over?*, which is in references.bib as `gebhardt2005stock` and is cited nowhere else. Same authors, same year, same journal, different result.

rows.name: Intermediate Momentum
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}11$ to $t{-}7$, excluding recent returns.

rows.name: Systematic Momentum (6-1)
rows.description: Sum of fitted values over months $t{-}5$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression (bond market factor).

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Momentum (6-1)
rows.description: Sum of residuals over months $t{-}5$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression (bond market factor).

rows.name: Industry Momentum (12-1)
rows.description: Equal-weighted average 12-1 momentum of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.

rows.name: Long-Term Reversal (48-12)
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}47$ to $t{-}12$. Uses expanding window starting at 12-3, ramping to 48-12.

rows.name: Long-Term Reversal (30-6)
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}29$ to $t{-}6$. Uses expanding window starting at 12-3, ramping to 30-6.

rows.name: Industry LTR (48-12)
rows.description: Equal-weighted average 48-12 LTR of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.

rows.name: Short-Term Reversal
rows.description: Prior month return $r_{t-1}$.

rows.name: 9-Month Momentum

rows.name: Systematic Momentum (3-1)
rows.description: Sum of fitted values over months $t{-}2$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression.

rows.name: Systematic Momentum (12-1)
rows.description: Sum of fitted values over months $t{-}11$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Momentum (3-1)
rows.description: Sum of residuals over months $t{-}2$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Momentum (12-1)
rows.description: Sum of residuals over months $t{-}11$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression.

rows.name: Industry Momentum (1)
rows.description: Equal-weighted average prior-month return of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.

rows.name: Industry Momentum (3-1)
rows.description: Equal-weighted average 3-1 momentum of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.

rows.name: Long-Term Reversal (24-3)
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}23$ to $t{-}3$. Uses expanding window starting at 12-3.

rows.name: Industry LTR (30-6)
rows.description: Equal-weighted average 30-6 LTR of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.

rows.name: Industry LTR (24-3)
rows.description: Equal-weighted average 24-3 LTR of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.

rows.name: Price Impact
rows.description: Pastor-Stambaugh liquidity: negated coefficient from return reversal regression on signed volume. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Amihud Illiquidity
rows.description: Within-month mean of daily $|r_t|/\text{dvol}_t$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Amihud Volatility
rows.description: Monthly standard deviation of daily Amihud ratios. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Roll Spread
rows.description: Implicit bid-ask spread: $2\sqrt{\max(-\text{Cov}(r_t, r_{t-1}), 0)}$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Roll Autocovariance
rows.description: Negative autocovariance of log returns $\times 100$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Relative Bid-Ask Spread
rows.description: Volume-weighted $(P^{ask} - P^{bid})/\text{mid}$. Requires a minimum of 5 prices.

rows.name: Corwin-Schultz Spread
rows.description: High-low spread estimator using two-day price ranges. Requires a minimum of 5 prices.

rows.name: Abdi-Ranaldo Spread
rows.description: Closing price spread estimator. Requires a minimum of 5 prices.

rows.name: No-Trade Day Proportion
rows.description: Fraction of business days with no valid price. Returns are never inspected, so the old name "Zero-Return Proportion" contradicted this description.

rows.name: FHT Spread
rows.description: Spread derived from zero-return proportion: $2\sigma\Phi^{-1}((1+p_{zro})/2)$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Volatility-over-Volume
rows.description: Liquidity proxy: $2.5 \times \sigma^{0.6} / \bar{V}^{0.25}$, where $\sigma$ is the volatility of daily RETURNS and $\bar{V}$ mean volume. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns. Not the volatility OF volume.

rows.name: Negative LIX (Illiquidity)
rows.description: $-\log_{10}[(V \times P_{\text{close}}) / (P_{\text{high}} - P_{\text{low}})]$. Requires a minimum of 5 prices. Stored NEGATED (lib/illiq_pandas.py), so it rises with ILLIQUIDITY -- 99.29% of non-null values are negative, median -2.181.

rows.name: Absolute Bid-Ask Spread
rows.description: Volume-weighted $(P^{ask} - P^{bid})$ in dollars. Requires a minimum of 5 prices.

rows.name: Daily Volatility
rows.description: Standard deviation of daily returns within the month.

rows.name: Daily Skewness
rows.description: Central skewness of daily returns within the month.

rows.name: Daily Kurtosis
rows.description: Excess kurtosis of daily returns within the month.

rows.name: Realized Volatility
rows.description: Within-month square root of sum of squared daily returns: $\sqrt{\sum r_t^2}$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Realized Signed Jump
rows.description: Within-month asymmetry in positive vs.\ negative squared returns: $(RV^+ - RV^-)/RV$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Realized Skewness
rows.description: Within-month third moment of daily returns scaled by realized volatility. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Realized Kurtosis
rows.description: Within-month fourth moment of daily returns scaled by realized volatility. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: 95% Value-at-Risk
rows.description: 5th percentile loss from empirical daily return distribution over a 36(12) rolling window.

rows.name: 90% Expected Shortfall
rows.description: Mean of worst 10% of daily returns over a 36(12) rolling window.

rows.name: 90% Value-at-Risk
rows.description: 10th percentile loss from empirical daily return distribution over a 36(12) rolling window.

rows.name: Systematic Volatility
rows.description: Standard deviation of systematic returns (CAPMB fitted values) within the month. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Volatility
rows.description: Standard deviation of idiosyncratic returns (CAPMB residuals) within the month. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Volatility (MKT)
rows.description: Residual volatility from joint MKTRF+MKTB regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Volatility (BBW)
rows.description: Residual volatility from BBW 4-factor regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Volatility (VP)
rows.description: Residual volatility from VOLPSB regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Skewness
rows.description: Skewness of residuals from coskewness regression.

rows.name: Equity Market Beta
rows.description: Beta on MKTRF from joint regression with MKTB (36-month rolling).

rows.name: Bond Market Beta
rows.description: Beta on MKTB from joint regression with MKTRF (36-month rolling).

rows.name: Bond Market Beta (Univariate)

rows.name: Duration-Adj Market Beta

rows.name: Term Premium Beta

rows.name: Upside Market Beta

rows.name: Term Beta

rows.name: Daily Market Beta
